methodological_rigor.justification: The design combines a retrospective 88-patient TNBC cohort (SCANDARE) analyzed by BayesPrism deconvolution with ex vivo tumor-on-chip experiments using multiple patient-derived primary ECM-myCAFs, two TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-436), two chemotherapies (doxorubicin, paclitaxel), siRNA silencing of G0S2, pan-kinase profiling, and pharmacologic SRC inhibition with dasatinib, yielding converging evidence. Controls are appropriate (monoculture vs coculture, DMSO vs drug, siCTRL vs siG0S2, CAP/CAF-S4 fibroblasts as a cell-type specificity control). Normality is checked by Shapiro-Wilk with parametric/non-parametric tests applied accordingly (Wilcoxon rank-sum/matched-pair, Mann-Whitney, Pearson chi-squared, Kolmogorov-Smirnov), but no a priori power calculation is reported, no explicit blinding of image scoring is described, multiplicity handling for scRNA-seq DEG and kinome analyses is only partially described, and some confirmatory experiments rely on only n=2 patient-derived CAFs (e.g., Fig. 2J-M, Fig. 7I). Overall rigor is solid for a mechanistic translational study with minor power/blinding gaps.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The core experimental claims (ECM-myCAF chemoprotection, SRC/G0S2 mechanism, dasatinib reversal) are preclinical and derive from in vitro/ex vivo tumor-on-chip coculture models with cell lines and primary CAFs, placing the evidence at Oxford LoE 5 despite the retrospective observational deconvolution of 114 TNBC samples. Clinical relevance is high because TNBC chemoresistance is a major unmet need, the mechanism points to a readily actionable, FDA-approved SRC-family inhibitor (dasatinib) combined with standard chemotherapies (doxorubicin, paclitaxel), and the SCANDARE correlation (ECM-myCAFs persist in chemoresistant tumors) provides patient-level support. Translational path remains speculative without in vivo models or clinical trial data, so the score is 4 rather than 5.

reporting_quality.justification: The study mixes an observational biobank cohort analysis with extensive preclinical ex vivo/in vitro mechanistic work; no single checklist fits perfectly (STROBE for the cohort component, ARRIVE not applicable as no animal work was performed), so 'other' is selected. Methods are thoroughly detailed: SCANDARE registration (NCT03017573), ethics approval (CPP Ile-de-France 3), inclusion criteria (RCB-based classification), antibody catalog/RRIDs, cell-line STR authentication, Mycoplasma testing, drug concentrations, 10x Genomics kit versions, Cell Ranger/Seurat/Harmony/BayesPrism/DoRothEA versions, and image analysis parameters. Data/code availability is not explicitly stated in the manuscript body visible here (no repository accessions, GEO IDs, or code links are mentioned), and the data-availability statement appears to have been redacted or omitted; this is a reproducibility gap, especially for the scRNA-seq and deconvolution analyses.

novelty_literature.justification: The novel contributions are: (i) demonstration that a specific CAF subset (ECM-myCAF) rather than CAFs globally mediates TNBC chemoresistance; (ii) identification of G0S2 as a required mediator of CAF-induced chemoresistance (G0S2 has not previously been linked to anticancer-therapy resistance per the authors); (iii) implication of SRC-family kinase activation upstream of G0S2 in cancer cells; and (iv) methodological application of tumor-on-chip with STAMP and CNN-based proximity analysis to deconstruct a 'kiss-of-life' priming event. Prior work from the same group had already defined ECM-myCAFs and their immunotherapy-resistance role (Kieffer 2020, Croizer 2024), and CAF-mediated chemoresistance is broadly known, so the biological framework is incremental; however, the specific molecular axis (ECM-myCAF -> SRC -> G0S2) and the actionable dasatinib rescue are new and fill a documented gap.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical introduction that positions ECM-myCAFs within prior CAF-heterogeneity literature, methods that are highly detailed, and a results section that builds a coherent patient-to-ex vivo-to-mechanism-to-rescue narrative. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (88 patients, 114 samples, specific drugs and findings) and self-contained, and figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, including sample sizes, statistical tests, and scale bars. The 'kiss-of-life' metaphor is memorable but slightly informal, and the abstract teaser line is repeated verbatim; some sentences in Introduction/Discussion are long. References are current and span mechanistic, methodological, and clinical literature.

key_strengths: Integrated patient-cohort deconvolution (88 patients, 114 samples) with ex vivo tumor-on-chip modeling using multiple patient-derived primary ECM-myCAFs, two TNBC cell lines, and two chemotherapies, yielding convergent evidence
Specificity controls (CAP/CAF-S4 fibroblasts have no chemoprotective effect) establish that the phenotype is CAF-subset-specific rather than a generic stromal effect
Mechanistic chain is closed by orthogonal perturbations: siRNA silencing of G0S2 abolishes CAF-mediated protection, and dasatinib (SRC inhibitor) rescues chemosensitivity
Novel identification of G0S2 as a CAF-driven mediator of TNBC chemoresistance, linked to SRC-family kinase activation and an actionable drug combination
Methods are reported in exhaustive technical detail (RRIDs, kit versions, pipeline versions, antibody dilutions, STR/Mycoplasma QC)
key_concerns: No a priori power/sample-size justification, no explicit blinding of manual video scoring, and some confirmatory experiments rely on only n=2 patient-derived CAFs
Data and code availability statements are not visible in the manuscript (no GEO/repository accessions or code links); scRNA-seq and deconvolution reproducibility is therefore limited

SRC-G0S2 causal direction is partially circular (G0S2 silencing lowers pSRC), and the proposed secreted ligands (HGF, FGF2) are inferred from scRNA-seq expression but not functionally validated with blocking antibodies/recombinant ligands
Lack of in vivo validation (xenograft or PDX) of the dasatinib-plus-chemotherapy rescue limits translational strength
Deconvolution-based inference of cancer-cell G0S2 expression from bulk RNA-seq (BayesPrism get.exp) warrants orthogonal validation (IHC/spatial) at the protein level in patient tissue
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically solid, mechanistically rich translational study with clear specificity controls and an actionable therapeutic implication; the content fits a strong Tier 2 oncology journal, with Tier 1 limited by the lack of in vivo validation and reliance on cell-line models for the mechanism.
